words.enDefinition: A hierarchical structure with one designated starting node called the root

examples.en: Our worksheet represented family relationships as a rooted tree with one starting point.
examples.zh: 练习表把亲属关系表示为有一个起点的「有根树」。

examples.en: We drew a rooted tree before examining the nodes below its top.
examples.zh: 我们先画了一棵「有根树」，再看顶部节点下方有哪些节点。

collocations: a rooted tree with three levels

words.enDefinition: The distinguished starting node of a tree that has no parent

examples.en: The traversal starts at the root node before exploring the children below.
examples.zh: 遍历从「根节点」开始，再探索下方的子节点。

examples.en: I marked the root node at the top of the diagram.
examples.zh: 我在图的顶部标出了「根节点」。

words.enDefinition: A tree node with no children

examples.en: The first search finished at a leaf node with no branches below.
examples.zh: 第一次查找在下方没有分支的「叶节点」结束。

examples.en: Our tutor marked each leaf node with a different colour in the tree.
examples.zh: 导师在树里用另一种颜色标出了所有「叶节点」。

words.enDefinition: A tree node that has at least one child

examples.en: The new child made the previously isolated leaf an internal node in the tree.
examples.zh: 添加子节点后，原来没有子节点的叶节点成了「内部节点」。

examples.en: I checked each internal node while tracing the search on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我在练习表上跟踪查找过程时，核对了每个「内部节点」。

collocations: an internal node with two children

words.enDefinition: A tree node one level above and directly linked to another

examples.en: We moved back to the parent node after finishing the left branch.
examples.zh: 走完左分支之后，我们回到了「父节点」。

examples.en: The diagram showed a parent node above two nodes at the same level.
examples.zh: 图上，同一层的两个节点上方有一个「父节点」。

collocations: a parent node with two children

words.enDefinition: A tree node linked directly below its parent in the structure

examples.en: I added a child node below the item we had just inserted.
examples.zh: 我在刚插入的项目下方添加了一个「子节点」。

examples.en: The traversal moved to a child node after printing the current key.
examples.zh: 遍历打印当前键之后，移到了一个「子节点」。

collocations: a child node of the root

words.enDefinition: A different tree node that shares the same immediate parent

examples.en: The sibling node shared a parent with the leaf we just visited.
examples.zh: 「兄弟节点」与我们刚访问的叶节点有同一个父节点。

examples.en: We drew a sibling node beside the original branch in the example.
examples.zh: 我们在示例原有分支旁画了一个「兄弟节点」。

collocations: compare keys with a sibling node

words.enDefinition: A node above a given node on its path toward the root

examples.en: The ancestor node was two levels above the selected leaf in our diagram.
examples.zh: 图里，「祖先节点」比我们选择的叶节点高两层。

examples.en: We followed the parent links until we reached the specified ancestor node.
examples.zh: 我们沿着父节点的链接往上走，直到到达指定「祖先节点」。

collocations: move up to an ancestor node

words.enDefinition: A node reachable by following one or more child links downward

examples.en: The deepest descendant node lay three levels below the node we selected.
examples.zh: 最深的「后代节点」比我们选的节点低三层。

examples.en: Our exercise marked every descendant node below the chosen internal node.
examples.zh: 我们的练习标出了指定内部节点下方的所有「后代节点」。

words.enDefinition: A tree formed by a node and all its descendants

examples.en: The search skipped a subtree whose keys were all too small.
examples.zh: 查找跳过了一棵键值全都太小的「子树」。

examples.en: We drew the subtree separately to see how many nodes remained.
examples.zh: 我们把「子树」单独画出来，看还有多少节点。

words.enDefinition: The number of edges from a tree's root to a node

examples.en: The node depth increased by one whenever we followed a child link.
examples.zh: 每沿一个子节点链接向下走，「节点深度」就增加一。

examples.en: We recorded node depth beside every marked node in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们在练习表标记过的每个节点旁记录了「节点深度」。

words.enDefinition: The length of a longest path from the root downward

examples.en: We measured tree height by counting edges along the longest downward path.
examples.zh: 我们通过数最长向下路径上的边来测量「树高」。

examples.en: The tree height grew after we added a child to the deepest leaf.
examples.zh: 我们给最深的叶节点加了一个子节点后，「树高」增加了。

words.enDefinition: A tree whose nodes have at most two ordered children

examples.en: Our binary tree had some nodes with only a right child.
examples.zh: 我们的「二叉树」里有些节点只有右子节点。

examples.en: The tutor drew a binary tree to illustrate left and right branches.
examples.zh: 导师画了一棵「二叉树」来说明左分支和右分支。

words.enDefinition: a binary tree in which the keys in each node's left and right subtrees follow the corresponding smaller and larger ordering rules

examples.en: We used a binary search tree to look up the numbers in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用「二叉搜索树」查找练习中的数字。

examples.en: Our binary search tree placed the smaller keys on the left at each step.
examples.zh: 我们的「二叉搜索树」在每个节点都把较小的键放到左侧。

collocations: insert a key into a binary search tree

words.enDefinition: A binary tree whose nodes have either zero or two children

examples.en: The full binary tree had two children at every node that was not a leaf.
examples.zh: 「严格二叉树」里的每个非叶节点都有两个子节点。

examples.en: We checked whether removing only one child still left a full binary tree.
examples.zh: 我们检查了只去掉一个子节点后，剩下的还是不是「严格二叉树」。

collocations: check for a full binary tree

words.enDefinition: A binary tree filled by levels, with any final gaps rightmost

examples.en: The complete binary tree had its last two nodes at the far left.
examples.zh: 「完全二叉树」最后一层的两个节点都在最左边。

examples.en: We checked the leftward placement of nodes in a complete binary tree.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「完全二叉树」中的节点是否靠左排列。

collocations: levels of a complete binary tree

words.enDefinition: A binary tree with two children per internal node and equally deep leaves

examples.en: Every leaf in the perfect binary tree appeared on the same bottom level.
examples.zh: 「完美二叉树」的所有叶节点都在最底下的同一层。

examples.en: We drew a perfect binary tree with all available positions completely filled.
examples.zh: 我们画了一棵填满所有可用位置的「完美二叉树」。

collocations: levels of a perfect binary tree

words.enDefinition: A tree where each internal node has only one child

examples.en: The insertion sequence produced a degenerate tree that looked like a chain.
examples.zh: 这个插入顺序产生了一棵看上去像链条的「退化树」。

examples.en: We counted every edge when tracing the degenerate tree from top to bottom.
examples.zh: 我们从上到下跟踪「退化树」时，数了每一条边。

collocations: a search in a degenerate tree

words.enDefinition: An ordered tree maintained to keep its height from growing excessively

examples.en: The balanced search tree kept its height small after we inserted several keys.
examples.zh: 我们插入多个键后，「平衡搜索树」仍维持较小的高度。

examples.en: Our lecturer compared a balanced search tree with an example shaped like a chain.
examples.zh: 老师把「平衡搜索树」与链条形状的示例作了比较。

collocations: insert into a balanced search tree

words.enDefinition: a binary search tree whose left and right subtree heights differ by at most one at each node

examples.en: Our AVL tree needed a rotation after we inserted the largest key.
examples.zh: 我们插入最大键后，这棵「AVL 平衡二叉树」需要旋转一次。

examples.en: The tutor used an AVL tree to illustrate a precise balance rule.
examples.zh: 导师用一棵「AVL 平衡二叉树」来说明一条明确的平衡规则。

words.enDefinition: The difference between the heights of two subtrees at a node

examples.en: The balance factor became zero after we added a child on the left.
examples.zh: 我们在左边加了一个子节点后，「平衡因子」变成了零。

examples.en: Our example defined the balance factor as left height minus right height.
examples.zh: 示例把「平衡因子」定义为左子树高度减去右子树高度。

words.enDefinition: A local rearrangement that preserves a search tree's in-order key sequence

examples.en: The tree rotation changed the shape without changing the order of the keys.
examples.zh: 「树旋转」改变了形状，键的顺序保持不变。

examples.en: We drew the tree rotation before checking whether the branches were balanced.
examples.zh: 我们先画出「树旋转」的过程，再检查分支是否平衡。

collocations: a tree rotation around a node

words.enDefinition: A systematic way of visiting nodes in a tree

examples.en: The tree traversal recorded the letters in the order the nodes were visited.
examples.zh: 「树遍历」按访问节点的顺序记录了字母。

examples.en: We compared two versions of the tree traversal using the same small diagram.
examples.zh: 我们用同一张小图比较了「树遍历」的两种方式。

collocations: the order of a tree traversal

words.enDefinition: A tree traversal visiting each node before its child subtrees

examples.en: The preorder traversal recorded the root label before the two branches below.
examples.zh: 「前序遍历」先记录根节点的标签，再记录下方的两个分支。

examples.en: We used preorder traversal to print the folder label before its contents.
examples.zh: 我们用「前序遍历」先打印文件夹标签，再打印里面的内容。

words.enDefinition: A binary tree traversal visiting left subtree, node, then right subtree

examples.en: The inorder traversal displayed the binary search tree's keys in increasing order.
examples.zh: 「中序遍历」按升序显示二叉搜索树中的键。

examples.en: We traced inorder traversal by writing the parent between its two subtrees.
examples.zh: 我们把父节点写在两棵子树之间，跟踪了「中序遍历」。

collocations: an inorder traversal of a binary tree

words.enDefinition: A tree traversal visiting child subtrees before the current node

examples.en: The postorder traversal processed the children before recording the parent's label.
examples.zh: 「后序遍历」先处理子节点，再记录父节点的标签。

examples.en: We used postorder traversal to add branch totals before computing the root value.
examples.zh: 我们用「后序遍历」先把分支合计相加，再计算根节点的值。

words.enDefinition: Visiting tree nodes level by level starting at the root

examples.en: The level-order traversal printed every second-level node before reaching the lower leaves.
examples.zh: 「层序遍历」先打印第二层的全部节点，再到下方的叶节点。

examples.en: Our whiteboard showed which row came next in the level-order traversal.
examples.zh: 白板显示了「层序遍历」接下来访问哪一行。

collocations: a level-order traversal of a tree

words.enDefinition: The value used to identify an item during a search

examples.en: I changed the search key and followed a different branch of the tree.
examples.zh: 我改了「查找键」，然后沿树的另一条分支继续找。

examples.en: The search key matched the value stored at the root in our example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「查找键」与根节点存的值相同。

collocations: compare a search key with a node's key

words.enDefinition: The number of nodes in a subtree rooted at a given node

examples.en: The subtree size increased when we attached another leaf beneath its root.
examples.zh: 我们在子树根节点下添加一片叶节点后，「子树大小」增加了。

examples.en: We recorded the subtree size next to the highlighted node on our diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在图中高亮的节点旁记录了「子树大小」。

words.enDefinition: The node visited immediately after another in an inorder traversal

examples.en: The inorder successor came from the right subtree in this example.
examples.zh: 这个示例中的「中序后继节点」来自右子树。

examples.en: We found the inorder successor by writing out the ordered list of keys.
examples.zh: 我们把键按顺序写成列表，找出了「中序后继节点」。

collocations: replace a node with its inorder successor

words.enDefinition: A tree storing sequences that share paths for common prefixes

examples.en: The trie used the same first branch for these two words.
examples.zh: 「字典树」给这两个单词共用了第一条分支。

examples.en: We inserted the three place names into the trie in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课上把三个地名插入了「字典树」。

collocations: insert a word into a trie

words.enDefinition: The deepest tree node containing both selected nodes in its subtree

examples.en: The lowest common ancestor was the parent shared by two neighbouring leaves.
examples.zh: 「最近公共祖先」是两个相邻叶节点共用的父节点。

examples.en: We found the lowest common ancestor by comparing the paths from the root.
examples.zh: 我们比较了从根节点出发的两条路径，找出了「最近公共祖先」。

collocations: a query for the lowest common ancestor

words.enDefinition: Searching an item collection sequentially for a specified target

examples.en: The linear search checked each name from the top of the list.
examples.zh: 「线性查找」从列表顶部开始逐一检查姓名。

examples.en: We used linear search because the exercise had only a few items.
examples.zh: 我们用了「线性查找」，因为练习只有几项数据。

collocations: use linear search on an unsorted list

words.enDefinition: Searching an ordered range by repeatedly discarding one half of it

examples.en: The binary search ruled out the smaller half after comparing the middle key.
examples.zh: 「二分查找」比较中间的键后，排除了较小的那一半。

examples.en: We tried binary search again after putting the dates in order.
examples.zh: 我们把日期排好序后，又试了一次「二分查找」。

collocations: implement binary search on sorted data

words.enDefinition: The part of an ordered sequence still considered during a search

examples.en: The search interval shrank after we compared the key with the middle item.
examples.zh: 我们把键和中间元素比较后，「查找区间」缩小了。

examples.en: Our diagram showed the search interval after each comparison in binary search.
examples.zh: 图里显示了二分查找每次比较后的「查找区间」。

words.enDefinition: The index chosen near the middle of the current search range

examples.en: We recalculated the midpoint index after discarding the left part of the list.
examples.zh: 排除列表左侧部分后，我们重新计算了「中点下标」。

examples.en: The value at the midpoint index was too large in this step.
examples.zh: 这一步里，「中点下标」处的值太大了。

words.zhGloss: 首个不小于目标值的查找
words.enDefinition: Finding the first position in sorted data whose value meets or exceeds target
acceptedZhAnswers: 首个不小于目标值的查找

examples.en: A lower-bound search stopped at the first equal value in our sorted list.
examples.zh: 「首个不小于目标值的查找」停在有序列表里第一个相等的值上。

examples.en: The lower-bound search returned the next larger value’s position when none matched exactly.
examples.zh: 没有完全相等的项时，「首个不小于目标值的查找」返回了下一个更大值的位置。

collocations: a lower-bound search for duplicate keys

words.zhGloss: 首个大于目标值的查找
words.enDefinition: Finding the first position in sorted data whose value exceeds the target
acceptedZhAnswers: 首个大于目标值的查找

examples.en: The upper-bound search passed all three copies of the target value.
examples.zh: 「首个大于目标值的查找」越过了三个与目标值相等的项。

examples.en: Our worksheet showed an upper-bound search ending just past the last duplicate.
examples.zh: 练习表里，「首个大于目标值的查找」在最后一个重复值之后结束。

collocations: an upper-bound search in sorted data

words.enDefinition: A position where adding a key preserves the current sorted order

examples.en: The search returned an insertion point for a name absent from the list.
examples.zh: 查找为列表中没有的姓名返回了「有序插入位置」。

examples.en: We drew the insertion point between two scores on the number line.
examples.zh: 我们在数轴上两个分数之间画出了「有序插入位置」。

collocations: insert a key at the insertion point

words.enDefinition: The field or value used to determine how items are ordered

examples.en: We used the submission date as the sorting key for the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在练习中用提交日期作为「排序键」。

examples.en: The list changed order when I replaced its sorting key with the title.
examples.zh: 我把「排序键」改成标题后，列表顺序变了。

collocations: sort records by a sorting key

words.enDefinition: A field used to order records whose primary sorting values match

examples.en: We used the first name as a secondary sort key after the surname.
examples.zh: 姓氏相同时，我们用名字作为「次级排序键」。

examples.en: The spreadsheet used a secondary sort key to distinguish records with identical scores.
examples.zh: 电子表格用「次级排序键」来区分同分记录。

collocations: a secondary sort key for ties

words.enDefinition: A sorting method that orders items by comparing their keys

examples.en: The worksheet used a comparison sort with alphabetically ordered names as keys.
examples.zh: 练习表采用「比较排序」，按姓名的字母顺序比较各键。

examples.en: We traced a comparison sort on five names from our practice roster.
examples.zh: 我们用练习名册里的五个姓名跟踪了「比较排序」。

collocations: the limits of a comparison sort

words.enDefinition: A sort preserving the original relative order of equal keys

examples.en: The stable sort preserved the original order of students with equal scores.
examples.zh: 「稳定排序」保留了同分学生的原有相对顺序。

examples.en: We chose a stable sort so entries with matching dates stayed in order.
examples.zh: 我们选了「稳定排序」，使日期相同的条目保持原有顺序。

collocations: check whether a sort is stable
choose a stable sort for duplicate keys

words.enDefinition: A sort rearranging items directly with little additional working storage

examples.en: The in-place sort rearranged values directly inside the existing array in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的示例中，「原地排序」直接在现有数组里重新排列值。

examples.en: Our tutor compared an in-place sort with a method needing a separate array.
examples.zh: 导师把「原地排序」和一种需要独立数组的方法作了比较。

collocations: the extra storage of an in-place sort

words.enDefinition: A sort that benefits when its input already has some order

examples.en: The adaptive sort made fewer comparisons once we nearly ordered the list.
examples.zh: 列表快排好时，「自适应排序」所做的比较更少。

examples.en: We tried an adaptive sort on dates already grouped into sorted runs.
examples.zh: 我们用「自适应排序」处理已经分成多个有序段的日期。

collocations: an adaptive sort on almost sorted data

words.enDefinition: Sorting by inserting successive items into an already ordered part

examples.en: The insertion sort moved the next card into the correct place.
examples.zh: 「插入排序」把下一张卡放到了正确位置。

examples.en: We tried insertion sort with a sequence that was nearly sorted already.
examples.zh: 我们用一组几乎已经排好序的数据试了「插入排序」。

collocations: use insertion sort on small inputs

words.enDefinition: Sorting by repeatedly selecting the smallest remaining item for the next position

examples.en: The selection sort put the smallest remaining score in the next position.
examples.zh: 「选择排序」把剩余最低分放到下一个位置。

examples.en: I counted the comparisons made by selection sort during the first pass.
examples.zh: 我数了「选择排序」在第一趟中作了多少次比较。

collocations: compare selection sort with insertion sort

words.enDefinition: Sorting through repeated passes that swap adjacent items out of order

examples.en: Our bubble sort moved the largest key to the end during its first pass.
examples.zh: 我们的「冒泡排序」在第一趟就把最大键移到了末尾。

examples.en: We checked whether bubble sort needed another pass after a round without swaps.
examples.zh: 一趟未发生交换后，我们检查了「冒泡排序」是否还需要继续。

words.enDefinition: Sorting by dividing input into parts and merging their sorted results

examples.en: We used merge sort to order the scores, then examined the final merge.
examples.zh: 我们用「归并排序」给分数排序，再观察最后一次归并。

examples.en: The merge sort example showed the separate lists before joining them.
examples.zh: 「归并排序」示例先显示各个列表，再把它们合起来。

words.enDefinition: Sorting by partitioning around a pivot and sorting the resulting parts

examples.en: Our quicksort split the list around a value chosen for comparison.
examples.zh: 我们的「快速排序」以一个选定的比较值为基准把列表划分开来。

examples.en: We compared the partitions made by quicksort on two different inputs.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「快速排序」对两种输入划出的各部分。

words.enDefinition: Sorting by building a heap and repeatedly removing its highest priority item

examples.en: The heapsort example built a heap before moving the largest values.
examples.zh: 「堆排序」示例先建立堆，然后才移出最大的值。

examples.en: We compared storage use for heapsort and a method with temporary lists.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「堆排序」和一种用临时列表的方法的存储用量。

words.enDefinition: Sorting by counting occurrences of each key within a limited range

examples.en: Our counting sort counted each score before writing the values in order.
examples.zh: 我们的「计数排序」先统计各分数的出现次数，再按顺序写出。

examples.en: The exercise used counting sort on ratings drawn from five possible values.
examples.zh: 练习用「计数排序」处理只有五种可能取值的评分。

collocations: the key range for counting sort

words.enDefinition: Sorting keys by successively grouping them according to individual digits or positions

examples.en: Our radix sort example grouped the numbers by their last digit first.
examples.zh: 我们的「基数排序」示例先按数字的最后一位分组。

examples.en: We traced radix sort using labels that all had the same length.
examples.zh: 我们用长度相同的标签跟踪了「基数排序」。

words.enDefinition: Sorting by distributing items into groups and combining ordered groups

examples.en: The bucket sort example put scores into groups before ordering each group.
examples.zh: 「桶排序」示例先把分数分组，再在组内排序。

examples.en: We chose ranges for bucket sort before placing the values into groups.
examples.zh: 我们先为「桶排序」选定值域，再把数值分到各组。

words.enDefinition: An ordered section of a sequence starting at its beginning

examples.en: The sorted prefix grew after we inserted one more name in order.
examples.zh: 把又一个姓名按顺序插入后，「已排序前缀」变长了。

examples.en: We underlined the sorted prefix before tracing the next insertion in class.
examples.zh: 课上跟踪下一次插入之前，我们给「已排序前缀」画了下划线。

words.enDefinition: A consecutive stretch of values already ordered within a sequence

examples.en: We found a sorted run within the list of partly ordered dates.
examples.zh: 我们在部分有序的日期列表中找到了一个「有序段」。

examples.en: The diagram showed a sorted run that ended just before a smaller key.
examples.zh: 图里有一个「有序段」，恰好在一个更小的键前结束。

words.enDefinition: A chosen value used to separate items during a partition

examples.en: The pivot element was the middle value in our first sorting example.
examples.zh: 我们的第一个排序示例用中间的值作为「枢轴元素」。

examples.en: I checked which items were smaller than the pivot element on the board.
examples.zh: 我在白板上检查了哪些项比「枢轴元素」小。

words.enDefinition: A stage separating items into groups according to a chosen criterion

examples.en: The partitioning step placed smaller keys together in the quicksort example.
examples.zh: 快速排序示例中的「划分步骤」把较小的键放到一组。

examples.en: We recorded both groups after completing the partitioning step on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 完成练习表上的「划分步骤」后，我们记录了两组数据。

words.enDefinition: The stage that combines sorted parts into one ordered result

examples.en: The merge step chose the next item from the front of either list.
examples.zh: 「归并步骤」从两个列表之一的开头选出下一项。

examples.zh: 我们把两半数据各自排好后，跟踪了「归并步骤」。

words.enDefinition: Arrange values from the smallest or earliest to the largest or latest

examples.en: The guide asked us to sort in ascending order before comparing the two lists.
examples.zh: 指南让我们先「按升序排列」，再比较两个列表。

words.enDefinition: A method splitting a problem into smaller parts and combining solutions

examples.zh: 我们的「分治算法」先解决两半的子问题，再合并两个结果。

words.enDefinition: The number of pairwise key comparisons made by an algorithm

examples.en: Our comparison count went up when the input arrived in reverse order.
examples.zh: 输入按相反顺序到来时，我们的「比较次数」增加了。

examples.zh: 我们记录了「比较次数」，另行统计交换次数。

words.enDefinition: An individual point in a graph that edges can connect

examples.zh: 图中用一个「顶点」表示地图上的每一站。

examples.en: We labelled each vertex before adding the connections between the rooms.
examples.zh: 我们先给各「顶点」贴上标签，再添加房间之间的连接。

words.enDefinition: A connection between two vertices in a graph

examples.zh: 我为连接两座楼的步道画了一条「图的边」。

examples.zh: 我们在课上删掉一条「图的边」，表示这条路已经关闭。

collocations: a graph edge between two vertices

words.enDefinition: A graph whose edges each have a specified direction

examples.en: The directed graph represented which course had to come before another.
examples.zh: 「有向图」表示哪门课必须排在另一门之前。

examples.en: We used arrows when drawing the directed graph on the board.
examples.zh: 我们画白板上的「有向图」时用了箭头。

collocations: represent dependencies in a directed graph

words.enDefinition: A graph whose edges connect endpoints without a specified direction

examples.en: The undirected graph represented walking routes that could be used either way.
examples.zh: 「无向图」表示可以双向通行的步行路线。

examples.zh: 我们绘制「无向图」时，每个连接用一条不带箭头的线表示。

collocations: an edge in an undirected graph

words.enDefinition: A graph with numeric values assigned to edges or connections

examples.en: We used a weighted graph to show different walking times between rooms.
examples.zh: 我们用「带权图」表示房间之间各不相同的步行时间。

examples.zh: 练习表里的「带权图」为可用路线赋了成本。

collocations: model travel in a weighted graph
an edge in a weighted graph

words.enDefinition: A graph where edges have no individual numeric costs

examples.en: The unweighted graph counted each connection as one step in the puzzle.
examples.zh: 解谜时，「无权图」把每个连接都计为一步。

examples.en: We used an unweighted graph when the time between rooms did not matter.
examples.zh: 房间之间的通行耗时不影响结果时，我们用「无权图」表示。

collocations: an example of an unweighted graph
shortest paths in an unweighted graph

words.enDefinition: A numeric value representing the cost or length of an edge

examples.en: The edge weight showed the number of minutes for one route segment.
examples.zh: 「边权」表示一段路线需要多少分钟。

examples.en: I changed an edge weight and recalculated the cheapest route on paper.
examples.zh: 我改了一个「边权」，在纸上重新计算了成本最低的路线。

words.enDefinition: A vertex directly connected to a specified vertex by an edge

examples.en: The search checked an adjacent vertex before moving farther across the diagram.
examples.zh: 搜索先检查一个「相邻顶点」，再向图中更远处移动。

examples.en: I marked the adjacent vertex on the other end of the connection.
examples.zh: 我在连接的另一头标出了「相邻顶点」。

collocations: an edge to an adjacent vertex

words.enDefinition: A graph representation storing the neighbours of each individual vertex

examples.en: Our adjacency list listed the neighbouring stops beside each named location.
examples.zh: 我们的「邻接表」在每个地点旁列出了相邻站点。

examples.en: I used the adjacency list to find which vertices could be visited next.
examples.zh: 我用「邻接表」查找接下来可以访问哪些顶点。

words.enDefinition: A table indexed by vertices indicating which pairs share edges

examples.en: The adjacency matrix had a row and column for every room.
examples.zh: 「邻接矩阵」为每个房间都设了一行和一列。

examples.en: We compared two entries in the adjacency matrix for the undirected example.
examples.zh: 我们比较了无向图示例里「邻接矩阵」中的两项。

words.enDefinition: A graph representation storing its edges as pairs of endpoints

examples.en: The edge list had one pair for each path in the diagram.
examples.zh: 「边列表」为图中每段路径记录了一对顶点。

examples.en: We converted the edge list into a record of neighbours for each vertex.
examples.zh: 我们把「边列表」转换为记录各顶点邻居的数据。

collocations: store weights in an edge list

words.enDefinition: A graph containing relatively few edges among its possible vertex pairs

examples.en: The sparse graph showed few routes between the many rooms in our example.
examples.zh: 示例里的房间很多，「稀疏图」只画出了少量相连的路线。

examples.en: We used a neighbour list for the sparse graph on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们用邻居列表表示练习表上的「稀疏图」。

collocations: an adjacency list for a sparse graph

words.enDefinition: A graph containing many edges relative to the possible connections

examples.en: The dense graph had connections between nearly every pair in the example.
examples.zh: 在这个示例中，「稠密图」几乎每对顶点都相连。

examples.en: We counted the marked entries when drawing the dense graph as a table.
examples.zh: 我们把「稠密图」画成表格后，数了表里标记过的项。

collocations: an adjacency matrix for a dense graph

words.enDefinition: The number of directed edges entering a specified vertex

examples.en: The course had an in-degree of two because two prerequisites pointed to it.
examples.zh: 两个先修课都指向这门课，所以这门课对应顶点的「入度」是二。

examples.en: We updated the in-degree after removing one incoming arrow in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课上删掉一条指入的箭头后，更新了「入度」。

words.enDefinition: The number of directed edges leaving a specified vertex

examples.en: The last task had an out-degree of zero in our diagram.
examples.zh: 图中最后一个任务顶点的「出度」为零。

examples.en: I counted the arrows leaving each point to find its out-degree.
examples.zh: 我数了从各点发出的箭头，求出各自的「出度」。

words.enDefinition: An edge whose source and destination are the same vertex

examples.en: The self-loop led back to the same room in our puzzle.
examples.zh: 在我们的谜题中，「自环」回到了同一个房间。

examples.en: We marked the self-loop before checking which links reached different rooms.
examples.zh: 我们先标出「自环」，再检查哪些连接通往别的房间。

words.enDefinition: Systematically exploring vertices and edges according to a selected search order

examples.en: The graph traversal recorded both the vertices and their discovery order.
examples.zh: 「图遍历」记录了顶点以及发现它们的顺序。

examples.en: We compared two methods of graph traversal using the same map.
examples.zh: 我们用同一张地图比较了两种「图遍历」方式。

words.enDefinition: A search exploring vertices in successive layers from the starting point

examples.en: Our breadth-first search visited all one-step neighbours before checking places farther away.
examples.zh: 我们的「广度优先搜索」先访问相距一步的所有邻居，再查看更远的位置。

examples.en: We used breadth-first search to count the fewest steps through the maze.
examples.zh: 我们用「广度优先搜索」计算走迷宫最少需要几步。

collocations: use breadth-first search for minimum hops

words.enDefinition: A search following a branch as far as possible before returning

examples.en: The depth-first search followed one branch until it could go no further.
examples.zh: 「深度优先搜索」沿一条分支前进，直到无法再深入。

examples.en: We drew the path taken by depth-first search through the small puzzle.
examples.zh: 我们画出了「深度优先搜索」在这个小游戏中经过的路径。

collocations: detect a cycle using depth-first search

words.enDefinition: Discovered vertices still waiting for their outgoing connections to be explored

examples.en: The search frontier contained two rooms after we explored the starting room.
examples.zh: 探索完起点房间后，「搜索前沿」中有两个房间。

examples.en: Our trace crossed out each vertex after removing it from the search frontier.
examples.zh: 我们在跟踪表里划掉从「搜索前沿」移出的每个顶点。

collocations: add a vertex to the search frontier

words.enDefinition: The collection marking vertices already discovered or processed during a search

examples.en: We checked the visited set before returning through the same doorway.
examples.zh: 我们穿过同一扇门返回前，先查了「已访问集合」。

examples.en: The visited set prevented the example from exploring the same vertices repeatedly.
examples.zh: 「已访问集合」让示例不会反复探索同样的顶点。

collocations: add a vertex to the visited set

words.enDefinition: A layer of vertices at the same minimum distance from the source

examples.zh: 两个房间都离起点两步，所以它们的「广度优先搜索层级」相同。

examples.en: I labelled the BFS level on the board before tracing the next layer.
examples.zh: 我在白板上标出「广度优先搜索层级」，再跟踪下一层。

collocations: vertices at the same BFS level

words.enDefinition: A sequential marker for when a search first discovers a vertex

examples.en: The tutor wrote each DFS discovery time beside the vertex in the diagram.
examples.zh: 导师在图中的顶点旁写上各自的「深搜发现时间戳」。

examples.en: We compared the DFS discovery time with the recorded completion marker for that vertex.
examples.zh: 我们把「深搜发现时间戳」和那个顶点记录的完成标记作了对照。

words.enDefinition: The recorded point when depth-first exploration of a vertex finishes

examples.en: We recorded the DFS finish time after exploring the vertex and its search descendants.
examples.zh: 完成该顶点及其搜索树后代的探索后，我们记录了「深搜完成时间戳」。

examples.en: We wrote the DFS finish time beside the point where the search returned.
examples.zh: 我们在图中的搜索返回处写了「深搜完成时间戳」。

collocations: order vertices by DFS finish time

words.enDefinition: in depth-first search, an edge from a node to an ancestor in the depth-first tree, including a self-loop where applicable

examples.en: The back edge pointed back to a vertex on our current path.
examples.zh: 「回边」指回我们当前路径上的一个顶点。

examples.en: Our tutor drew a back edge while discussing cycle detection in directed graphs.
examples.zh: 导师讲有向图的环检测时，画了一条「回边」。

collocations: a cycle indicated by a back edge

words.enDefinition: deciding whether a graph contains a cycle, a path that returns to its start without other repeated vertices

examples.en: We used cycle detection to check for circular prerequisites in the sample.
examples.zh: 我们用「环检测」查找示例里的循环先修关系。

examples.en: The worksheet applied cycle detection before trying to put the tasks in order.
examples.zh: 练习表先做了「环检测」，再尝试给任务排序。

words.enDefinition: A maximal group of mutually reachable vertices in an undirected graph

examples.zh: 我们把从入口可达的所有房间归到同一个「连通分量」。

examples.zh: 步行桥损坏后，地图上桥的两侧各形成一个独立「连通分量」。

examples.en: The isolated room was an unreachable vertex when we started outside.

examples.zh: 距离表里「不可达顶点」对应的一项留空了。

examples.en: The reachability query gave a different result after one directed link was removed.
examples.zh: 删去一条有向连接后，「可达性查询」给出了不同结果。

words.enDefinition: A directed graph with no route forming a directed cycle

examples.zh: 在简化示例中，课程要求组成了一个「有向无环图」。

examples.en: We drew a directed acyclic graph before putting its tasks into order.
examples.zh: 我们先画了一个「有向无环图」，再给图上的任务排序。

words.enDefinition: Ordering vertices so each directed edge points from earlier to later

examples.en: The topological sort put all prerequisite tasks before the tasks requiring them.
examples.zh: 「拓扑排序」把所有前置任务排在依赖它们的任务之前。

examples.en: We tried a topological sort after checking the dependency diagram for cycles.
examples.zh: 我们先检查依赖关系图中有没有环，再试做「拓扑排序」。

examples.zh: 我在迷宫里数了三条边，得出「路径长度」。

examples.en: The path length changed after the exercise removed the shortest connection.
examples.zh: 练习移去最短的连接后，「路径长度」变了。

examples.zh: 练习把「所有点对的最短路径」放在以两个端点为索引的表里。

examples.en: We calculated all-pairs shortest paths to compare routes from any stop on our map.
examples.zh: 我们计算了「所有点对的最短路径」，方便比较地图上从任意站点出发的路线。

solve an all-pairs shortest paths problem

words.enDefinition: The chosen starting vertex for computing distances or exploring connections

examples.en: The source vertex represented the entrance at the north end in our example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「源顶点」表示北端的入口。

examples.en: We changed the source vertex before repeating the shortest path calculation.
examples.zh: 重新计算最短路径前，我们换了「源顶点」。

examples.en: The path cost increased after we added a slower section to the route.
examples.zh: 我们给路线加了一段速度较慢的路后，「路径代价」增加了。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the path cost by adding the numbers on each edge.
examples.zh: 导师把路径上各边的数字相加，核对了「路径代价」。

words.enDefinition: The best distance found so far before it is confirmed

examples.en: The tentative distance fell when we found a shorter route through another room.
examples.zh: 我们找到一条经由另一房间的更短路线后，「暂定距离」降低了。

examples.zh: 处理下一个顶点前，我抄下了各地点的「暂定距离」。

examples.zh: 课上，一次「边松弛」降低了最后一个顶点记录的距离。

examples.zh: 我们通过查看新路线是否代价更低来跟踪「边松弛」。

words.enDefinition: a mapping recording a previous vertex for reached vertices other than the source where a path has been found

examples.en: The program updated the predecessor map after finding a shorter path to the exit.
examples.zh: 程序找到通往出口的更短路径后，更新了「前驱映射表」。

examples.en: We used the predecessor map to trace the route backwards to the source.
examples.zh: 我们用「前驱映射表」反向追踪这条路径，直到回到源顶点。

words.enDefinition: Recovering an ordered route from stored search results or links

examples.en: The exercise used path reconstruction after working out the distance to the exit.
examples.zh: 练习先计算到出口的距离，再做「路径重建」。

examples.en: We started path reconstruction at the destination and followed each link backwards.
examples.zh: 我们从目的地开始「路径重建」，沿各连接反向追踪。

examples.en: We applied Dijkstra's algorithm to a map whose walking times were all positive.
examples.zh: 我们把「迪杰斯特拉算法」用于步行耗时都为正数的地图。

examples.en: The worksheet showed the next vertex chosen by Dijkstra's algorithm during the search.
examples.zh: 练习表显示了搜索时「迪杰斯特拉算法」选定的下一个顶点。

words.enDefinition: A shortest-path method allowing negative weights and detecting reachable negative cycles

examples.en: The Bellman-Ford algorithm accommodated a negative edge weight in our classroom puzzle.
examples.zh: 「贝尔曼福特算法」适用于我们课堂谜题中的一个负边权。

examples.en: We traced the Bellman-Ford algorithm after adding an edge with a negative cost.
examples.zh: 加了一条代价为负的边后，我们跟踪了「贝尔曼福特算法」。

examples.en: The example assigned a negative edge weight to the edge representing a rebate.
examples.zh: 示例给表示返还额的那条边赋了一个「负边权」。

examples.en: We checked whether a negative edge weight affected the choice of algorithm.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「负边权」是否会影响算法选择。

words.enDefinition: A cycle whose edge weights sum to less than zero

examples.en: The distance fell on every repetition through the same negative cycle in class.
examples.zh: 课上，每重复经过同一个「负权环」一次，距离就再减少。

examples.en: I added the edge weights to check for a negative cycle.
examples.zh: 我把边权相加，检查是否存在「负权环」。

collocations: a graph containing a negative cycle

words.enDefinition: An all-pairs shortest-path method that progressively allows more intermediate vertices

examples.en: The Floyd-Warshall algorithm filled a distance table for every pair of locations.
examples.zh: 「弗洛伊德沃舍尔算法」填写了各地点两两之间的距离表。

examples.en: We watched the Floyd-Warshall algorithm update its entries after considering a new intermediate vertex.
examples.zh: 我们观察了「弗洛伊德沃舍尔算法」在考虑一个新的中间顶点后更新各项。

words.enDefinition: A route search prioritising travelled cost plus estimated remaining cost

examples.en: We traced A* search on the classroom maze before comparing the paths.
examples.zh: 比较路径前，我们先在课堂迷宫里跟踪了「A星搜索」。

examples.en: The straight-line distance was an admissible heuristic for the walking-distance exercise.
examples.zh: 直线距离在步行距离练习中是一个「可采纳启发式估计」。

examples.en: The minimum spanning tree connected all the rooms with the lowest total walkway cost.
examples.zh: 「最小生成树」用总成本最低的步道连接了所有房间。

examples.en: We compared two graphs before finding a minimum spanning tree for each one.
examples.zh: 我们先比较了两个图，再分别求出各自的「最小生成树」。

collocations: the weight of a minimum spanning tree

words.enDefinition: Growing a spanning tree by repeatedly choosing its lightest edge to outside vertices

examples.en: We traced Prim's algorithm from a chosen starting vertex on the board.
examples.zh: 我们在白板上从选定的起点跟踪了「普里姆算法」。

collocations: an edge chosen by Prim's algorithm

examples.en: The example used Kruskal's algorithm to consider edges in increasing weight order.
examples.zh: 示例用「克鲁斯卡尔算法」按权重升序考虑各边。

examples.zh: 在执行「克鲁斯卡尔算法」时，我们跳过了一条会产生环的边。

examples.en: We used asymptotic analysis to compare how two methods scaled with larger inputs.
examples.zh: 我们用「渐近分析」比较两个方法处理更大输入时资源开销的增长情况。

examples.zh: 导师先介绍「渐近分析」，再在课上比较画出的增长曲线。

words.enDefinition: Notation giving an upper growth bound up to constant factors

examples.en: The worksheet expressed the upper bound using big O notation beside the graph.
examples.zh: 练习表在图旁用「大O记号」表示上界。

examples.en: I used big O notation after counting the comparisons for a larger input.
examples.zh: 我数完较大输入所需的比较次数后，用了「大O记号」。

collocations: express a bound using big O notation
compare functions using big O notation

words.enDefinition: Notation giving a lower growth bound up to constant factors

examples.en: The lecturer used big Omega notation when writing the comparison lower bound.
examples.zh: 老师写比较次数的下界时，用了「大Ω记号」。

examples.en: We expressed the minimum growth rate using big Omega notation in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们用「大Ω记号」表示最低增长速度。

collocations: write a lower bound in big Omega notation
express comparison counts in big Omega notation

words.enDefinition: Notation giving matching upper and lower growth bounds up to constants

examples.en: We used big Theta notation after establishing both bounds for the same function.
examples.zh: 我们确定同一函数的上下界后，用「大Θ记号」表示。

examples.en: Our worksheet compared big Theta notation with a statement giving only an upper bound.
examples.zh: 我们的练习表把「大Θ记号」与只给出了上界的表述作了比较。

collocations: state a tight bound in big Theta notation
express growth in big Theta notation

words.enDefinition: The quantity used to measure how much data an algorithm receives

examples.en: We defined input size as the number of records for this exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把练习中的「输入规模」定义为记录的数量。

examples.en: The input size grew when we added more vertices to the example graph.
examples.zh: 我们给示例图加了更多顶点后，「输入规模」增大了。

words.enDefinition: The smallest running cost among inputs of a fixed size

examples.en: Our best-case running time came from matching the first item examined in the list.
examples.zh: 我们的「最好情况运行时间」来自列表第一项就匹配成功的情形。

examples.en: We calculated best-case running time before counting the work for other inputs.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「最好情况运行时间」，再统计其他输入需完成的工作。

words.enDefinition: The largest running cost among inputs of a fixed size

examples.en: Our worst-case running time estimate assumed the algorithm checked every element in the list.
examples.zh: 我们估算「最坏情况运行时间」时，假设算法检查了列表中的每个元素。

examples.en: The class compared worst-case running time for two search methods at equal input sizes.
examples.zh: 全班比较了两种查找方法处理相同输入规模时的「最坏情况运行时间」。

words.enDefinition: Expected running cost under a stated distribution of possible inputs

examples.en: We stated a distribution before calculating average-case running time for the search.
examples.zh: 计算搜索算法的「平均情况运行时间」前，我们先说明了输入分布。

examples.en: The example gave each possible position equal weight when estimating average-case running time.
examples.zh: 示例估算「平均情况运行时间」时，给每个可能的位置相同的权重。

collocations: an assumption about average-case running time

words.enDefinition: Extra working storage an algorithm uses beyond its given input

examples.en: The example counted a temporary array as auxiliary space in the exercise.
examples.zh: 示例把一个临时数组计入练习的「辅助空间」。

examples.en: We compared auxiliary space before choosing a sort for the memory exercise.
examples.zh: 我们先比较「辅助空间」，再为内存练习选择排序算法。

words.enDefinition: A running cost bounded independently of the input size

examples.en: The course model treated reading one known array position as constant time.
examples.zh: 课程模型把读取一个已知数组位置视为「常数时间」操作。

examples.en: We checked whether the lookup still took constant time as inputs grew.
examples.zh: 我们检查了输入变大时，查找是否仍用「常数时间」。

words.enDefinition: A running cost growing proportionally to a logarithm of input size

examples.en: Binary search took logarithmic time in the comparison model used during class.
examples.zh: 在课上的比较次数模型中，二分查找需要「对数时间」。

examples.en: The exercise used logarithmic time to describe a process repeatedly halving inputs.
examples.zh: 练习用「对数时间」描述不断把输入减半的过程。

words.enDefinition: A running cost growing proportionally to the number of input items

examples.en: Scanning every score once took linear time in our simple classroom model.
examples.zh: 在课堂简化模型里，将每个分数扫描一遍需要「线性时间」。

examples.en: We found that adding another full pass still took linear time.
examples.zh: 我们发现，再增加一趟完整扫描所需的仍是「线性时间」。

collocations: sort in linear time under specified assumptions

words.enDefinition: A running cost proportional to the square of the input size

examples.en: Checking every pair of scores took quadratic time in the class example.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，检查每对分数需要「二次时间」。

examples.en: Our tutor used a square grid to illustrate how quadratic time grows.
examples.zh: 导师用方形网格说明「二次时间」下工作量如何增长。

words.enDefinition: a property established before a loop and preserved through every iteration

examples.en: Our loop invariant stated that the prefix already processed was in order.
examples.zh: 我们的「循环不变式」说明，已处理的前缀是有序的。

examples.en: We checked the loop invariant again after moving one more item.
examples.zh: 再移动一项后，我们重新验证了「循环不变式」。

words.enDefinition: Reasoning that an algorithm must eventually stop on allowed inputs

examples.en: The termination argument showed that the search interval shrank on every iteration.
examples.zh: 「终止性论证」说明，每轮迭代都会缩小查找区间。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for a termination argument after checking what the loop preserved.
examples.zh: 导师检查了循环保持的性质之后，要求给出「终止性论证」。

collocations: a termination argument for a loop

words.enDefinition: The guarantee of correct results if the algorithm eventually stops

examples.en: We checked partial correctness before asking whether the algorithm always finished.
examples.zh: 我们先检查「部分正确性」，再问算法是否一定能结束。

examples.en: The worksheet separated partial correctness from the argument that execution eventually ends.
examples.zh: 练习表把「部分正确性」与执行最终会结束的论证分开列出。

words.enDefinition: The guarantee that an algorithm terminates and meets its specification

examples.en: The final proof combined two arguments to show total correctness for the loop.
examples.zh: 最后的证明合并两个论证，说明该循环满足「完全正确性」。

examples.en: For total correctness, we needed to show that execution terminated on every allowed input.
examples.zh: 为证明「完全正确性」，我们需要说明每种有效输入都能让程序结束。

words.enDefinition: the property that an optimal solution can be built using optimal solutions to relevant subproblems

examples.en: The tutor used optimal substructure to combine shorter optimal routes into a solution.
examples.zh: 导师利用「最优子结构」把较短区段的最优路线组合成解。

examples.en: We checked for optimal substructure before choosing an approach for the scheduling task.
examples.zh: 选择排程任务的解决办法前，我们检查它是否有「最优子结构」。

words.enDefinition: Smaller problems that recur when solving different parts of a task

examples.en: The diagram highlighted overlapping subproblems that appeared on more than one branch.
examples.zh: 图中标出了在不止一条分支上出现的「重叠子问题」。

examples.en: We recognised overlapping subproblems when two choices led to the same smaller task.
examples.zh: 两个不同选择通向同一个较小任务时，我们认出了「重叠子问题」。

words.enDefinition: Solving a problem by storing and combining answers to smaller subproblems

examples.en: We used dynamic programming to reuse counts of shorter routes in the maze.
examples.zh: 我们用「动态规划」复用迷宫中较短路线的计数结果。

examples.en: The tutor introduced dynamic programming with a table for a route-counting puzzle.
examples.zh: 导师用一张路线计数谜题的表格介绍了「动态规划」。

collocations: solve a problem with dynamic programming

words.enDefinition: Saving computed subproblem results for reuse when the same inputs recur

examples.en: The memoization example reused an answer when the same subproblem appeared again.
examples.zh: 「记忆化」示例在同一个子问题再次出现时复用了答案。

examples.en: We compared the number of calls before and after adding memoization.
examples.zh: 我们比较了添加「记忆化」前后的调用次数。
